heuristics: R: the random-function premise on the adder walk on classes (i.i.d. uniform class data, independent of x and the coins; the class map is algebraic on top). Conditional statements used are theorems of R by deferred decisions (proof.md section 2.2), including L-ori (T2). R gives neither the successor distribution nor the birthday count.

H-coll: the birthday premise of section 2.1, unconditional: P(C_T = 0) <= exp(-(1 - eps) tau), with C_T the number of other-trail merges and eps = 0.00406911 = 0.00015286 + 2^-8. It models the random-mapping product bound (Flajolet and Odlyzko 1990; Teske 2001; Bernstein and Lange 2012). Declared, not derived from R.

H-merge′: the averaged successor premise of section 2.2, over the whole run and other trails only: E[M_T] <= (1 + 2^-8) sum_t E|V_o(t)|/N and E[N_T] <= (1 + 2^-8) sum_t E|V_nr(t)|/N. Own-trail successors, forced returns and 2-cycles are excluded. Declared, not derived from R; no conditional or singleton form is assumed.

H3: Callgrind instruction counts on production inputs represent the common path: 808.67 (plain) and 818.66 (anchor) instructions per walk step, plus at most 2 for the canon_pick branch (C_COMMON = 821), with the rare paths out of line and charged at worst case; the Markov reserve covers the expected rare work.
limitations: R is measured only marginally (non-equal share 1/6 on fresh windows, A = 8 to 1024); conditional laws are theorems of R, not measurements (proof.md section 4).
Analytic production cost; no production-size execution. Needs about 2^67.7 stored distinguished points; not a practical attack.
Field arithmetic is the package's own inline assembly, tested against Python big integers, not formally verified.
R is an unproved heuristic, not established at production size: the toy runs use theta = 2^-5, the formal test 6 adder bits and theta = 2^-6.
Rare-path charges are forced-path maxima from a bounding build (proof.md section 8.1), not proved for every input.
The exact-k fallback rate (2^-55 per canon call, section 6) follows from R and is not measured; no fallback occurred in the measured steps.
Escape depths are at most TRAIL_MAX (section 2.3); the order-of-2 check (section 2.4) needs only the assertions in accounting.py.
A replay cut-off (65n steps) fails the run and is counted in DELTA_CUT (proof.md sections 1.3 and 3).
The measurement harness reuses restart starts from a 1024-point pool (measurement/step.c); the algorithm draws fresh coins and is charged its cost (section 2.5).
Model success bound 0.410304 at tau = 0.5303 with eps = 0.00406911, 0.0203 above 0.39; the pooled toy-curve success is in the evidence.
Distinguished points never occur in a production-size sample; restart and abandonment paths were checked on small builds.
The probe cost (2^11 per probe) and the draw cost (2^16 per draw) are allowances, not measurements (sections 8.2 and 10).
H-coll and H-merge′ are declared premises with tolerance 2^-8, not measured at production size, and H-merge′ is not derived from R. The success bound stays at least 0.39 for tolerance up to 0.018.
The useful-merge bound (section 2.8) is DELTA_NR, about 1.1e-16, in expectation under H-merge′.
Sampling caps (D = 4) and the probe cap (L = 2^10) abort the run; their probabilities are in delta (sections 1.3, 8.2). The toy experiment retries identity starts without a cap.
The meter's expectation, and so the 1/64, is taken in R and H-merge′. A model-free rare-work bound costs about 10.9 bits (time_log2 about 137.4 instead of 126.5) and is not taken.
